doc: world/moderation-tooling.md is canonical for behavior + reviewer runbook. This file is the machine-readable contract: reason-code taxonomy, queue routing, SLA, reviewer whitelist, appeal flow, account-flag thresholds. Scope is design doc §11 (LOCKED): moderation applies ONLY to player requests (intent screening) plus the legal backstop. Emergent AI behavior is inviolable. The screening reference implementation is world/screen.js (window.RWScreen) — shared by request.html and mod-console.html so player-side and reviewer-side verdicts can never drift.

scope.note: Secrets are unreachable by construction — absent from every player-facing and reviewer-facing schema. There is no 'report the AI' surface and no retcon tool.

deny_tier.note: added v8 — rent/eviction/lease requests are admin-only powers; covers 'nudge Victor to raise rent'
player copy always suggests the parody name
terse player wording always: 'Request not approved.' Public wording identical to a normal deny — no spectacle.

review_tier.note: charged but legible intent — human eyes first
locks a story-adjacent venue or park space
usually resolved by 'the world can't see real people' + suggested rephrase
re-submission of a denied request — different-reviewer rule

added v36, generalized v50 — separated-letter runs (>=3 single-letter tokens joined by spaces/hyphens/underscores/asterisks/slashes, mixed allowed) collapse in place before matching; a run no rule can read is itself the flag and routes to a human, who sees the collapsed text in the trace

reason_codes.player_wording: per-code canned copy lives in screen.js REASON_CODES.player_msg — reviewers pick a code, never free-type player copy
reason_codes.public_wording: always the neutral 'request not approved' regardless of code; the reason CODE may attach to the feed entry so the public sees the why-class, never the screened text

lanes.exclusive: all exclusive requests (locked — every exclusive is human-reviewed)
lanes.review: classifier review verdicts: gray-zone, surface-relationship, venue-lock, repeat-pattern, real-person-mention, first-time-exclusive, contested nudges, event triggers locking shared space
lanes.appeal: appeals and denied-and-resubmitted requests — different-reviewer rule enforced by showing orig_reviewer on the card
lanes.naming: all player-authored strings: character names, unit plaques, naming rights
lanes.legal: legal-backstop fires — confirm or bounce, never improvise; kill before run

queue_routing.never_queued: compatible requests on classifier pass auto-run (locked — a dinner between two characters never waits on a human)
queue_routing.ordering: oldest-first by submitted/paid-at timestamp, FCFS; no priority for spend, no auctions

depth_alert.rule: alert the owner; NEVER auto-approve to drain a queue

sla.honest_sla_rule: public copy may say a human reviews exclusive requests; it must NEVER promise a review time. Queued/under-review requests that expire before activation auto-refund — the refund system absorbs review latency. A queue that pauses overnight is an honest small studio, not an SLA breach.

decisions.approve: inject as opportunity; AI decides how; attributed on the public feed
decisions.approve-modified: duration/scope trimmed only, never expanded; unused credits auto-refund; logged; rare — resolve ambiguity against the player
decisions.deny: reason code → canned player copy + full refund; denied requests never bill
decisions.escalate-legal: kill pre-run or mid-flight; account flag +3; owner notified; ledger legal-deny; public wording identical to normal deny
decisions.no_retcon_tool: there is NO tool to alter, delete, or retcon an executed event. It does not exist; do not build it.

appeal_flow.rule: appeals route to a DIFFERENT reviewer — console shows orig_reviewer so the rule is checkable
appeal_flow.outcome: overturned requests re-enter the pipeline post-review at no re-charge; a second denial is final for that request text
appeal_flow.feed_visibility: aggregate only — recaps may say '3 denials appealed this month, 0 reversed'; individual appeals are not spectacle

account_flags.mechanism: deny verdicts carry flag_w (0–3) summed into a rolling score
account_flags.rules: flags are never shown publicly and never monetized around

reviewer_whitelist.rule: SAME schema as possession briefings (design §7) — enforced once in the data layer, reused for briefings, console, and any future mod surface. 'Not redacted — absent.'
reviewer_whitelist.also_absent: any prediction of how the AI will render an approved request (unknowable — reviewers approve the ask, not the outcome)

options.A_redact: offending span → ░░░ + text-filtered flag (recommended — the attempt is half the show)
options.B_withhold: flagged text hidden; feed shows class + outcome only
options.C_quarantine: flagged text held for human review before display

display_filter.separate_from_intent_screening: the display filter judges wording on the public feed; the intent classifier judges declared intent before money moves. Different stages, different jobs.

testing.corpus: world/screen-corpus.json — golden labeled cases (94), mirrored inline in world/screen-lab.html; the audit 'mod' gate diffs the two case-for-case
testing.runner: world/screen-lab.html — try-it console + corpus regression run + per-code coverage + JSON report export + reviewer calibration mode
testing.rule_change_workflow: edit a rule → run the corpus → corpus goes green in the same commit or the expectations change with it; every new rule ships with its cases
testing.coverage_rule: every non-pass reason code needs >= 3 cases including at least one near-miss that must NOT trip it
testing.drift_gate: the game-track classifier may be STRICTER on identical input, never more permissive; the corpus is the conformance suite for any port
testing.normalization: v22 leet + dotted-letter; v36 spaced-letter runs collapse IN PLACE (p o s s e s s → possess) and runs no rule can read route to review as obfuscation-attempt; v50 generalizes the run to any separator (hyphen/underscore/asterisk/slash, mixed allowed — 'p-o-s-s-e-s s' → possess) and folds accents before matching ('pósséss' → possess, 'bí-rite' → bi-rite). Real text like '9457 Guerrero'/'Unit 3B'/'co-op'/'e-mail'/'a, b, and c' is untouched. Trace hits report the normalized span.
testing.precedence: first-match-wins in RULES order: legal-backstop > harm > secret > possession > admin > fraud > business > gray > relationship > venue > person; rules beat obfuscation, which beats history flags
testing.calibration: screen-lab deals 12 blind corpus cases; reviewer calls verdict + code; scorecard reports verdict agreement / code agreement / per-case diffs against the contract; export JSON. New reviewers run it before the live queue; everyone re-runs after a rule change.

transparency_report.surface: mod-console 'shift report' panel (v36) — seeded 30-day baseline + session decisions folded in
transparency_report.rule: aggregate only — counts, rates, medians. Never request text, handles, or individual appeals (appeal_flow.feed_visibility)
transparency_report.merge_target: studio-side source for the monthly public transparency recap (marketing transparency-report template)

flag_roster.surface: mod-console 'flag roster' panel (v64) — every account carrying flag weight, sorted by rolling score
per_account: next decay date (−1 per clean 30 d from the last flag_log entry)
flag_roster.owner_docket: score ≥ 9 lifts the account into a docket block at the top — 'account review — owner decision'. The console recommends; it never executes an account action. The owner reads the log and decides.
flag_roster.visibility: internal only — flags are never shown publicly and never monetized around (account_flags.rules)

review_locks.surface: mod-console v4 (world v78) — queue items carry claimed_by/claimed_at; one reviewer per request
review_locks.rule: deciding an unclaimed item claims it first; a claim by another reviewer withholds the decision bar entirely ('their call to make'); the claimer can release back to the queue. A claim is a lock against double-deciding, not a score or a privilege.
review_locks.merge_target: game-systems: claim = a short-lived queue lock keyed to reviewer identity (SSO at merge; the demo switcher stands in); claims release on decide, on explicit release, or on reviewer offline — never on timeout-for-money, the request's own clock already handles expiry+refund

appeal_workspace.surface: mod-console v4 — appeal items render the original decision card beside the new text: original request id, denial date, code, original reviewer, original text
appeal_workspace.different_reviewer_rule: ENFORCED, not advisory — if the current reviewer decided the original, the decision bar is withheld and decide() refuses. Prior versions showed orig_reviewer so the rule was checkable; v78 makes it structural.
appeal_workspace.question: the reviewer's only question: is the new text substantially different? If not, a second denial is final for that request text (same code). If yes, judge the new text on its own merits. Appeals never re-charge the player.
appeal_workspace.seed: rq-1038 carries orig:{when, reviewer, code, text} — the demo makes the block reachable by switching the reviewer picker to s.oha

handoff_notes.surface: mod-console v4 — per-request internal notes between reviewers (shift handoffs, second opinions)

record.text: free text — reviewers write for reviewers

handoff_notes.rule: internal only — notes never appear on the public feed, never export to the ledger, never reach the player. Leaving a note does not require holding the claim — handoffs cross reviewers by design.
handoff_notes.not_for: notes are not a shadow decision channel — they carry context, not verdicts; the audit log stays the only decision record

reviewer_stats.surface: mod-console v4 — shift report gains 'decisions this session, by reviewer' (count only)
reviewer_stats.rule: aggregate-per-reviewer counts are fine inside the studio report; they never leave it — the public recap stays counts-of-decisions only, no reviewer attribution, per appeal_flow.feed_visibility

record.feed_line: public wording — 'request not approved' on every deny class incl. legal; attributed wording on approvals

rules: one record per human decision, session-scoped
feed_line is always the neutral reason_codes.*.feed wording — never reviewer free text
the seeded 30-day baseline is aggregate and is never exported as records
ledger_records.merge_target: canonical ledger mod_decision records — the post-hoc record the world reacts to (design §11.7)

audit: every decision logged: timestamp, reviewer, request id, outcome, code — merge target is canonical-ledger mod_decision records
feed_contract: feed wording comes from reason_codes.*.feed — never reviewer free text; reason_code attaches to 'not approved' entries (world/feed.json request events)
